summary: In this fiction excerpt, a man walks with Ria across a campus of oversized red maples hung with a Swiss Family Robinson-style walkway. She describes the company's low-churn culture and her own off-campus, lone-gun status. He then confronts her angrily for letting Brautigan take his job and exile him to Siberia, just before he meets Viktor, a long-lived Great Old One.
one_line: A man and Ria stroll through a quirky treetop-walkway campus before he angrily confronts her about Brautigan taking his job, ahead of meeting Viktor.
key_facts: The company is bringing its other holdings around the world in line with HQ as fast as it can.
Churn at the company is described as incredibly low.
The company puts people back out into the world for a year every decade so they can see what it's like.
Ria says she has always lived off campus and commutes, calling herself 'not a team person' but a 'lone gun'.
The campus has oversized red maples with a suspended walkway of rope railings and platforms with baskets on pulleys.
Ria says the walkways' delightfulness never wears off 'for a certain kind of person'.
The twig-chair bench made of birch branches, rope and wire looks fragile but is very well built and barely gives under weight.
Ria says Viktor's schedule is his own, and if they are five minutes late someone will put five minutes' worth of useful 'injecta' into his in-box.
An engineer named Caleb, living in Vierzon, is mentioned as an example of someone who would supply that injecta.
The narrator accuses Ria of going along with Brautigan scooping his job and exiling him to Siberia.
The narrator calls the envoys 'absolute monarchs at Ate' who could have stopped it with a word.
The narrator is now a minister without portfolio about to meet one of the Great Old Ones in his vat; the man might live to be a thousand.
